s: Persistent bidirectional connection manager enabling real-time push from server to client over a single upgraded HTTP connection.
w: After HTTP upgrade handshake, both client and server send frames on the same TCP connection. The gateway manages millions of long-lived connections, routing messages to the correct backend service via connection registries (userId -> connectionId mappings). Heartbeats detect dead connections; reconnection with session resume handles network drops. Backpressure handles slow clients by buffering or dropping stale messages.
use: Live notifications: order status, collaboration cursors, alerts
Financial ticker feeds and live dashboards
avoid: Request/response patterns where HTTP/REST is simpler and stateless
Fan-out to millions of anonymous users without connection affinity (use SSE or polling)
Stateless serverless backends (persistent connections need persistent servers)

props.heartbeat_interval_ms: How often to ping idle connections
props.max_connections: Per-instance connection ceiling before load balancing

pat.d: Gateway subscribes to a message bus and pushes to connected clients by subscription.

pits: Connection storms on mass reconnect after gateway restart - stagger jitter on reconnect timers
Memory exhaustion from idle connections without heartbeat eviction
Load imbalance across gateway instances without connection-aware routing
tips: WebSocket is persistent bidirectional; SSE is one-way server-push - know the distinction
Connection count matters more than RPS for sizing - memory per connection is the constraint
